questions.response: write the answer and show the required work
questions.prompt: A circle of radius r is cut into many equal sectors, which are rearranged as shown. Explain why this shows that the area of the circle is πr².
questions.prompt_markup: A circle of radius r is cut into many equal sectors, which are rearranged as shown. Explain why this shows that the area of the circle is πr².
questions.correct_answer: Area = (half the circumference) × r = πr · r = πr².
questions.required_method: Describe the base and height of the rearranged shape and what happens as the number of sectors grows.
questions.grading_note: Any valid explanation. Essential: the shape approaches a parallelogram (rectangle); its height approaches r; its base is half the circumference, πr; area = πr · r = πr². Invalid: "the formula says so" or measuring one drawing.

questions.prompt: A circle of radius r is cut into many thin rings, like the layers of an onion. Each ring is cut open and straightened into a thin strip, and the strips are stacked from shortest (at the top) to longest (at the bottom). Explain why the stack approaches a triangle and why its area is πr².
questions.prompt_markup: A circle of radius r is cut into many thin rings, like the layers of an onion. Each ring is cut open and straightened into a thin strip, and the strips are stacked from shortest (at the top) to longest (at the bottom). Explain why the stack approaches a triangle and why its area is πr².
questions.correct_answer: The strips have lengths 2π · (distance from the center), from about 0 to 2πr, and the stack is r tall, so it approaches a triangle with base 2πr and height r: ½ · 2πr · r = πr².
questions.required_method: Find the lengths of the shortest and longest strips and the height of the stack.
questions.grading_note: Any valid explanation. Essential: strip length grows in proportion to the distance from the center; outer strip 2πr; height r; triangle area ½bh = πr².

questions.prompt: Use similarity to explain why the area of a circle of radius r equals r² times the area of a circle of radius 1. Then use the fact that the unit circle has area π to write the formula.
questions.prompt_markup: Use similarity to explain why the area of a circle of radius r equals r² times the area of a circle of radius 1. Then use the fact that the unit circle has area π to write the formula.
questions.correct_answer: A dilation by r multiplies every area by r², so A = r² · (area of the unit circle) = πr².
questions.required_method: A circle of radius r is a dilation of the unit circle by factor r; describe what a dilation does to areas.
questions.grading_note: Any valid explanation. Essential: circles are similar; areas scale by k²; the unit circle's area is π; A = πr².

questions.prompt: A quarter circle of radius 10 is drawn on a grid of unit squares. Counting full squares and estimating the partial ones gives about 78.5 squares. Explain how this supports A = πr² and why counting is evidence rather than proof.
questions.prompt_markup: A quarter circle of radius 10 is drawn on a grid of unit squares. Counting full squares and estimating the partial ones gives about 78.5 squares. Explain how this supports A = πr² and why counting is evidence rather than proof.
questions.correct_answer: The whole circle covers about 4 × 78.5 = 314 squares, and π · 10² ≈ 314.2, which agrees. Counting is approximate and checks one circle only, so it supports but does not prove the formula.
questions.grading_note: Any valid explanation. Essential: the scaled-up count (about 314); comparison with 100π; evidence versus proof.

questions.prompt: Explain why the area of a circle of radius r is more than 2r² and less than 4r², using an inscribed square and a circumscribed square, and check that πr² fits these bounds.
questions.prompt_markup: Explain why the area of a circle of radius r is more than 2r² and less than 4r², using an inscribed square and a circumscribed square, and check that πr² fits these bounds.
questions.correct_answer: The circumscribed square has side 2r (area 4r²); the inscribed square has diagonal 2r (area 2r²); the circle lies between them, and 2r² < πr² ≈ 3.14r² < 4r².
questions.required_method: Find the area of each square in terms of r.
questions.grading_note: Any valid explanation. Essential: both square areas from r (diagonal 2r gives area ½(2r)²); the circle is between them; 2 < π < 4.

questions.standard_level: Geometry. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Geometry, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.response: write the answer and show the required work
questions.prompt: A regular n-gon is inscribed in a circle of radius r. Its area is ½ · perimeter · apothem. Explain why this approaches πr² as n increases.
questions.prompt_markup: A regular n-gon is inscribed in a circle of radius r. Its area is ½ · perimeter · apothem. Explain why this approaches πr² as n increases.
questions.correct_answer: The perimeter approaches 2πr and the apothem approaches r, so the area approaches ½ · 2πr · r = πr².
questions.required_method: Describe what the perimeter and apothem approach.
questions.grading_note: Any valid explanation. Essential: perimeter → circumference; apothem → radius; substitution.
